9.solution: Only gases count: no gaseous product and 2 mol of gaseous reactants, so \(\Delta n = 0 - 2 = -2\).

12.solution: A conjugate base is the acid minus one \(\mathrm{H^+}\). One coordinated water loses a proton and becomes \(\mathrm{OH^-}\), and the charge drops by one: \([\mathrm{Zn(H_2O)_3OH}]^+\).

13.solution: Tin goes from \(+2\) to \(+4\) (oxidation) while iron goes from \(+3\) to \(+2\) (reduction).

14.solution: Hydrogen makes up about three quarters of the ordinary matter in the universe, making it the most abundant element.

16.solution: The chain has six carbons, numbered from the COOH carbon as C-1, with double bonds starting at C-2 and C-4: hexa-2,4-dienoic acid.

17.solution: The inductive effect is a permanent displacement of \(\sigma\) electrons along a chain: (A) - (IV). Hyperconjugation is delocalisation of C-H \(\sigma\) electrons into an adjacent p orbital or \(\pi\) bond: (B) - (III). The resonance effect is delocalisation of \(\pi\) electrons: (C) - (I).

18.solution: Friedel-Crafts alkylation joins an alkyl halide to benzene with anhydrous \(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\): \(\mathrm{C_6H_6 + CH_3Cl \rightarrow C_6H_5CH_3 + HCl}\). With \(\mathrm{CH_3COCl}\) it is acylation instead.

19.solution: Diamagnetic substances are weakly repelled by a magnetic field, so statements (B) and (D) are false. Paramagnetic substances are weakly attracted and ferromagnetic ones strongly attracted, so (A) and (C) are true.

20.solution: \(\rho a^3\) is the mass of one unit cell, so \(1.625\) g holds \(\dfrac{1.625}{3.25 \times 10^{-22}} = 5 \times 10^{21}\) unit cells. A bcc cell has 2 atoms, so there are \(1.0 \times 10^{22}\) atoms.

21.solution: In silica every Si is covalently bonded to four O atoms in a continuous three-dimensional network, a covalent (network) crystal. Fe is metallic, solid \(\mathrm{CH_4}\) molecular and KCl ionic.

23.solution: For large molecules the other colligative effects are tiny, but the osmotic pressure is still measurable at room temperature, so it gives their molar masses most precisely (and without heating, which could damage proteins).

28.solution: Each rate is divided by its stoichiometric coefficient, with a minus sign for reactants: rate \(= -\dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[A]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{3}\dfrac{d[C]}{dt} = \dfrac{d[D]}{dt}\). Only (D) matches.

29.solution: A thin film is nanoscale only in its thickness and extends in the other two dimensions, so it is classed as a two-dimensional nanostructure.

30.solution: A catalyst provides an alternative path with lower activation energy. It does not change the enthalpy of reaction.

31.subtopic: Colloids, Classification, Coagulation and Hardy-Schulze Rule
31.solution: A positive sol is coagulated by anions, and by the Hardy-Schulze rule the power rises steeply with the anion's charge. \(\mathrm{NO_3^-}\) has the lowest charge (\(-1\)), so \(\mathrm{KNO_3}\) is the weakest coagulant.

32.solution: Acid strength of the chlorine oxoacids rises with the oxidation state of Cl (more O atoms stabilise the anion). HOCl (Cl at \(+1\)) is the weakest and \(\mathrm{HClO_4}\) the strongest.

33.subtopic: Inner Transition Elements, Lanthanoids and Actinoids
33.solution: Ytterbium is \([\mathrm{Xe}]4f^{14}6s^2\), with a full 4f subshell. La is \(4f^0\), Eu \(4f^7\) and Gd \(4f^7 5d^1\).

34.subtopic: Colour, Magnetic Properties and Spin-Only Formula
34.solution: \(\mathrm{Sc^{3+}}\) is \(3d^0\), with no d electrons for d-d transitions, so its compounds are colourless. \(\mathrm{Ni^{3+}}\), \(\mathrm{Cr^{3+}}\) and \(\mathrm{V^{3+}}\) have partly filled d subshells.

35.subtopic: Bonding Theories, EAN, Crystal Field, Hybridization and Magnetism
35.solution: \([\mathrm{Co(NH_3)_6}]^{3+}\): low-spin \(d^6\), 0 unpaired. \([\mathrm{CoF_6}]^{3-}\): \(\mathrm{F^-}\) is weak field, high-spin \(d^6\), 4 unpaired. \([\mathrm{NiCl_4}]^{2-}\): tetrahedral \(d^8\), 2 unpaired. \([\mathrm{Ni(CN)_4}]^{2-}\): square planar \(d^8\), 0 unpaired. \([\mathrm{CoF_6}]^{3-}\) has the most.

36.subtopic: Bonding Theories, EAN, Crystal Field, Hybridization and Magnetism
36.solution: In the spectrochemical series \(\mathrm{Cl^- < H_2O < NH_3 < CN^-}\), so cyanide produces the largest crystal field splitting.

37.solution: Grignard reagents are prepared in dry ether, which has no acidic hydrogen and stabilises the reagent by coordinating to Mg. Alcohols, phenols and ketones would destroy it.

38.solution: In \(\mathrm{S_N2}\) the nucleophile attacks as the leaving group departs, through a single transition state in which the carbon is partly bonded to five groups. It gives inversion, not racemisation, and forms no carbocation.

39.solution: In a benzylic halide such as \(\mathrm{C_6H_5CH_2Cl}\), the halogen is on the \(\mathrm{CH_2}\) carbon next to the ring, which is \(sp^3\) hybridised.

40.solution: Making an alkyl fluoride by heating an alkyl bromide or chloride with a metallic fluoride such as \(\mathrm{Hg_2F_2}\) or AgF is the Swarts reaction.

41.subtopic: Chemical Reactions of Alcohols and Acidity
41.solution: Oxidation of a secondary alcohol gives a ketone: propan-2-ol, \(\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH_3}\), gives propanone. Propan-1-ol gives propanal and butan-2-ol gives butanone.

42.solution: Phenol with chloroform and aqueous NaOH gives salicylaldehyde (ortho-formylation): the Reimer-Tiemann reaction.

43.solution: In Williamson synthesis an alkoxide reacts with an alkyl halide. With the same alkyl groups it gives a simple ether, with different groups a mixed ether, so both kinds can be made.

44.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
44.solution: The electron-withdrawing Cl stabilises the carboxylate ion, so chloroacetic acid is stronger than formic, acetic and propanoic acids, whose alkyl groups (or H) do not.

45.solution: \(\mathrm{C_3H_9N}\) can be propylamine (\(1^\circ\)), ethylmethylamine (\(2^\circ\)) or trimethylamine (\(3^\circ\)). A quaternary ammonium salt has four carbon groups on a positive N plus an anion, so it cannot have this formula.

46.solution: A is true: protein amino acids are L. B is true: every amino acid has both groups. C is false: acidic amino acids such as aspartic acid have two COOH groups and basic ones such as lysine two \(\mathrm{NH_2}\) groups. D is true: tyrosine was first isolated from cheese (its name comes from the Greek for cheese).

47.solution: Denaturation breaks the hydrogen bonds and other weak forces that hold the folded shape, destroying secondary, tertiary and quaternary structure. The peptide bonds survive, so the primary structure (amino acid sequence) is unchanged.

48.solution: Ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is found in citrus fruits such as oranges and lemons.

49.solution: Bakelite is a phenol-formaldehyde resin. Formaldehyde is methanal, so the monomers are phenol and methanal.

50.solution: Novolac is a phenol-formaldehyde polymer, with no ester links. Glyptal, PHBV and Dacron are all polyesters.

51.solution:
\(\dfrac{1}{\log_a y} = \log_y a\), so the sum is \(\log_y(x + z) + \log_y(z - x) = \log_y(z^2 - x^2)\).

Since \(x^2 + y^2 = z^2\), \(z^2 - x^2 = y^2\) and the sum is \(\log_y y^2 = 2\).

53.solution:
The two end seats take two of the girls in \({}^3P_2 = 6\) ways. The third girl must avoid seats 2 and 8 (next to the ends), so she has seats 3 to 7: 5 choices. The boys fill the other 6 seats in \(6! = 720\) ways.

Probability \(= \dfrac{6 \times 5 \times 720}{9!} = \dfrac{21600}{362880} = \dfrac{5}{84}\).

54.subtopic: Selections with Conditions — At Least, At Most, Included and Excluded
54.solution:
16 balls are distinct. Taking k of the 7 identical balls (\(k = 0\) to 7) and \(12 - k\) distinct ones, the count is \(\displaystyle\sum_{j=5}^{12}{}^{16}C_j = 4368 + 8008 + 11440 + 12870 + 11440 + 8008 + 4368 + 1820 = 62322\).

\({}^{18}C_6 + {}^{18}C_8 = 18564 + 43758 = 62322\), which is option (A).

56.solution: Multiplying repeatedly by \(2\sin\theta\): the product equals \(\dfrac{\sin 32\theta}{32\sin\theta}\). With \(33\theta = \pi\), \(\sin 32\theta = \sin(\pi - \theta) = \sin\theta\), so the value is \(\dfrac{1}{32}\).

58.subtopic: Forms of a Line, Intersections and Concurrency
58.solution: The lines meet at \(\left(-\dfrac{2}{5}, -\dfrac{14}{5}\right)\). The line through it and \((0, 5)\) has slope \(\dfrac{5 + 14/5}{2/5} = \dfrac{39}{2}\), so \(y = \dfrac{39}{2}x + 5\), that is \(39x - 2y + 10 = 0\).

59.subtopic: Joint Equation of Two Lines — Product of Linear Factors and the Triangle They Form
59.solution: With \(y = 3 - x\): \(x^2 - 3x(3 - x) + (3 - x)^2 = 5x^2 - 15x + 9 = 0\). The sum of the x-coordinates is 3, so the midpoint has \(x = \dfrac{3}{2}\) and \(y = 3 - \dfrac{3}{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}\).

60.subtopic: Tangents — At a Point, With a Given Slope, From an External Point and Their Loci
60.solution: The centre \((7, -1)\) is \(\sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}\) from the origin and the radius is 5. If \(2\theta\) is the angle between the tangents, \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{5}{5\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), so \(\theta = 45^\circ\) and the angle is \(90^\circ\).

61.solution:
A tangent to \(y^2 = 4x\) is \(y = mx + \dfrac{1}{m}\). Its distance from \((3, 0)\) must be 3: \(\left(3m + \dfrac{1}{m}\right)^2 = 9(1 + m^2)\), which gives \(\dfrac{1}{m^2} = 3\), \(m = \pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).

For \(m = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) the contact point on the parabola is \(\left(\dfrac{1}{m^2}, \dfrac{2}{m}\right) = (3, 2\sqrt{3})\), above the X-axis. The tangent is \(y = \dfrac{x}{\sqrt{3}} + \sqrt{3}\), that is \(\sqrt{3}y = x + 3\).

63.subtopic: Logical Equivalence and Algebra of Statements
63.solution:
First remove the implication: \(\sim(p \wedge \sim q) \vee (q \wedge \sim p)\). The dual swaps \(\wedge\) and \(\vee\): \(\sim(p \vee \sim q) \wedge (q \vee \sim p) = (\sim p \wedge q) \wedge (q \vee \sim p) = \sim p \wedge q\).

Option (B): \((p \to q) \wedge \sim(q \to p) = (\sim p \vee q) \wedge (q \wedge \sim p) = q \wedge \sim p\). It matches.

64.solution: \(\sim(p \to q) \equiv p \wedge \sim q\): the hypothesis holds and the conclusion fails. "An integer is greater than 4 and less than 5 but it is not a multiple of 3."

65.subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Sine, Cosine and Projection Rules
65.solution:
Sine rule in triangles ABD and ACD: \(\dfrac{BD}{\sin\angle BAD} = \dfrac{AD}{\sin B}\) and \(\dfrac{DC}{\sin\angle CAD} = \dfrac{AD}{\sin C}\).

So \(\dfrac{\sin\angle BAD}{\sin\angle CAD} = \dfrac{BD}{DC}\cdot\dfrac{\sin B}{\sin C} = \dfrac{1}{3}\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt{3}/2}{1/\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{3}\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\).

66.subtopic: Solution of Triangle — Half-Angle Formulas, Napier's Analogy and Area
66.solution:
\(P_1 = \dfrac{2\triangle}{a}\), so the sum is \(\dfrac{a\cos A + b\cos B + c\cos C}{2\triangle}\).

\(a\cos A + b\cos B + c\cos C = R(\sin 2A + \sin 2B + \sin 2C) = 4R\sin A\sin B\sin C\) and \(\triangle = 2R^2\sin A\sin B\sin C\). The sum is \(\dfrac{4R}{4R^2} = \dfrac{1}{R}\).

\(1 \pm \sin 2x = (\cos x \pm \sin x)^2\), so near \(x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\) the root is \(\dfrac{\cos x + \sin x}{\cos x - \sin x} = \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + x\right)\), positive there.

So \(y = \dfrac{\pi}{4} + x\) and \(\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 1\).

\(\cos\dfrac{19\pi}{4} = \cos\dfrac{3\pi}{4} = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\). The argument is \(\dfrac{-1/\sqrt{2} - 1}{1/\sqrt{2}} = -(1 + \sqrt{2})\).

Since \(\tan\dfrac{3\pi}{8} = 1 + \sqrt{2}\), the value is \(-\dfrac{3\pi}{8}\).

76.solution:
A line with equal intercepts has slope \(-1\), so the tangent has slope 1. \(18yy' = 3x^2\) gives \(y' = \dfrac{x^2}{6y} = 1\), so \(y = \dfrac{x^2}{6}\).

Then \(9\dfrac{x^4}{36} = x^3\), so \(x = 4\) and \(y = \dfrac{16}{6} = \dfrac{8}{3}\). (Points with \(x = -4\) are not on the curve.)

77.solution: \(\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt} = -k\cdot 4\pi r^2\), so \(\dfrac{dr}{dt} = -k\): the radius falls uniformly. It falls 2 cm in 4 months, 0.5 cm per month, so 3 cm is gone in 6 months.

79.solution:
\(\sin^6 x + \cos^6 x = 1 - 3\sin^2 x\cos^2 x\), so the integrand is \(\dfrac{1}{\sin^2 x\cos^2 x} - 3 = \sec^2 x + \mathrm{cosec}^2 x - 3\).

The integral is \(\tan x - \cot x - 3x + c\).

80.solution:
Put \(x = a\tan^2\theta\). Then \(\sqrt{\dfrac{a + x}{x}} = \dfrac{\sec\theta}{\tan\theta} = \mathrm{cosec}\,\theta\), so the integrand is \(\theta\), and \(dx = 2a\tan\theta\sec^2\theta\,d\theta\).

By parts: \(\displaystyle\int\theta\cdot 2a\tan\theta\sec^2\theta\,d\theta = a\theta\tan^2\theta - a\int\tan^2\theta\,d\theta = a\theta\tan^2\theta - a\tan\theta + a\theta + c\).

81.solution: \(|\sin 2x|\) repeats every \(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\), and \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin 2x\,dx = 1\). Over \([0, \pi]\) the integral is \(2\).

82.solution: \(f(x)\sin x\) is odd and integrates to zero over \([-2, 2]\). \(\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{2}|x|\,dx = 2\int_0^2 x\,dx = 4\).

83.solution: The region is two right triangles with legs 1 and 1 (from \(x = 3\) to 4 and from 4 to 5), each of area \(\dfrac{1}{2}\): total \(1\) sq. unit.

84.solution:
Put \(v = x + y\): \(\dfrac{dv}{dx} = 1 + \sin v + \cos v = 2\cos^2\dfrac{v}{2}\left(1 + \tan\dfrac{v}{2}\right)\).

\(\displaystyle\int\dfrac{\frac{1}{2}\sec^2\frac{v}{2}}{1 + \tan\frac{v}{2}}\,dv = x + c\) gives \(\log\left[1 + \tan\dfrac{x + y}{2}\right] = x + c\).

85.solution: \(\left(\dfrac{d^3y}{dx^3}\right)^{7/3} = 3 - \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^5\). Cubing removes the fractional power: \(\left(\dfrac{d^3y}{dx^3}\right)^7 = \left[3 - \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^5\right]^3\). Order 3, degree 7.

86.solution:
Separating: \(\dfrac{y + 1}{y}\,dy = -e^x(\cos^2 x - \sin 2x)\,dx\). Since \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(e^x\cos^2 x) = e^x(\cos^2 x - \sin 2x)\), integrating gives \(y + \log y = -e^x\cos^2 x + c\).

At \(x = 0\), \(y = 1\): \(1 = -1 + c\), so \(c = 2\): \(\log y + y + e^x\cos^2 x = 2\).

87.solution: A vector in the plane is \(\lambda(1, 1, 2) + \mu(1, 2, 1)\). Perpendicular to \((1, 1, 1)\): \(4\lambda + 4\mu = 0\), so \(\mu = -\lambda\) and the vector is along \((0, -1, 1)\). The unit vectors are \(\pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(\hat{j} - \hat{k})\).

89.subtopic: Scalar Triple Product, Coplanarity, and Volume
89.solution:
\(\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = (1\cdot(-1) - 1\cdot 4,\ 1\cdot 2 - 1\cdot(-1),\ 1\cdot 4 - 1\cdot 2) = (-5, 3, 2)\), with magnitude \(\sqrt{38}\) (the base area).

Volume \(= |(\vec{a} \times \vec{b})\cdot\vec{c}| = |-5 + 3 + 6| = 4\). Altitude \(= \dfrac{4}{\sqrt{38}} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{19}}\) units.

90.solution:
The area of a quadrilateral is \(\dfrac{1}{2}|\overline{AC} \times \overline{BD}|\), with \(\overline{BD} = \vec{b} - \vec{a}\).

\((3\vec{a} + 2\vec{b}) \times (\vec{b} - \vec{a}) = 3\vec{a} \times \vec{b} - 2\vec{b} \times \vec{a} = 5\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\). Area \(= \dfrac{5}{2}|\vec{a} \times \vec{b}|\), so \(\alpha = \dfrac{5}{2}\).

92.solution: Points on the line: \((3 - 5t, 5 - 4t, -7 + 15t)\). The YOZ plane has \(x = 0\), so \(t = \dfrac{3}{5}\): \(y = 5 - \dfrac{12}{5} = \dfrac{13}{5}\) and \(z = -7 + 9 = 2\).

93.solution:
Equate coordinates: \(1 + 2\lambda = 4 + 5\mu\), \(m + 3\lambda = 1 + m\mu\), \(3 + 4\lambda = \mu\).

From the first and third: \(1 + 2\lambda = 4 + 15 + 20\lambda\), so \(\lambda = -1\) and \(\mu = -1\). Then \(m - 3 = 1 - m\), giving \(m = 2\).

94.solution:
The lines pass through \((-1, 3, 1)\) and \((0, 1, 2)\), with directions \((1, -\lambda, \lambda)\) and \((1, 2, -2)\) (doubling \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, 1, -1\right)\)).

Coplanar: \(\begin{vmatrix} 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 1 & -\lambda & \lambda \\ 1 & 2 & -2 \end{vmatrix} = 1(2\lambda - 2\lambda) + 2(-2 - \lambda) + 1(2 + \lambda) = -2 - \lambda = 0\), so \(\lambda = -2\). (Then the two lines are parallel, and parallel lines are coplanar.)

The ball starts at \(30^\circ\) above the horizontal, so its horizontal velocity is \(v\cos 30^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}v\), which stays constant.

114.solution: By Wien's law \(\lambda_m T\) is constant, so T becomes \(\dfrac{3}{2}T\). Power \(\propto T^4\), so it grows by \(\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^4 = \dfrac{81}{16}\).

Let the open pipe's fundamental be n. Its first overtone is 2n. Closed at one end (same length), the fundamental is \(\dfrac{n}{2}\) and the second overtone is \(5 \times \dfrac{n}{2} = \dfrac{5n}{2}\).

\(\dfrac{5n}{2} - 2n = \dfrac{n}{2} = 100\), so \(n = 200\) Hz.

For a thin prism \(\delta = (n - 1)A\). In air \(\delta_1 = \left(\dfrac{3}{2} - 1\right)A = \dfrac{A}{2}\).

In the liquid the relative index is \(\dfrac{3/2}{1/3} = \dfrac{9}{2}\), so \(\delta_2 = \left(\dfrac{9}{2} - 1\right)A = \dfrac{7A}{2} = 7\delta_1\).

144.solution:
\(eV = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi\) and \(\dfrac{eV}{12} = \dfrac{hc}{6\lambda} - \phi\). Multiplying the second by 12: \(eV = \dfrac{2hc}{\lambda} - 12\phi\).

Equating: \(\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi = \dfrac{2hc}{\lambda} - 12\phi\), so \(\phi = \dfrac{hc}{11\lambda}\) and the threshold wavelength is \(11\lambda\).
